chunks: ʿAlī, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ibn Udhaynah, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar (عليه السلام), who said:

Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) descended to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) with two pomegranates from Paradise. He gave them both to him, so he ate one of them and split the other into two halves. He gave ʿAlī (عليه السلام) half of it, and he ate it. Then he said: “O ʿAlī, as for the first pomegranate that I ate, it is prophethood, and you have no share in it; and as for the other, it is knowledge, so you are my partner in it.”

key_terms.النُّبُوَّةُ: prophethood, reserved exclusively for the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله)
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise, the heavenly source of the two pomegranates
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: divinely granted knowledge shared by the Prophet with Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام)
key_terms.جَبْرَئِيلُ: Jibrāʾīl, the angelic messenger who brought the heavenly gift
key_terms.رَسُولِ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah, recipient of revelation and prophethood
key_terms.شَرِيكِي: my partner, indicating shared participation in knowledge

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe Imam ʿAlī’s (عليه السلام) share in the Prophet’s knowledge?
ai.summary: This hadith describes Jibrāʾīl (عليه السلام) bringing two pomegranates from Paradise to the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله), one representing prophethood and the other representing knowledge. The Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) states that Imam ʿAlī (عليه السلام) has no share in prophethood, but is his partner in knowledge, highlighting his unique rank in receiving the Prophet’s knowledge.
